title: CRJA/194/2008 of RAVI DAS Vs STATE

paras.text:
1
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Jail Appeal No. 194 of 2008
Ravi Das
S/o Ramesh Das
R/o Tagor Nagar, Shakti Farm
P.S. Sitarganj, District Udham Singh Nagar
 ................... Appellant

..........Respondent
Mr. G.S.Negi, Advocate ( Amicus Curiae), present for the appellant.
Shri Hari Om Bhakuni, Brief Holder, present for the State.
Hon'ble Prafulla C. Pant, J.

This appeal, moved on behalf of the accused
Ravi Das got sent through Superintendent District
Jail Dehradun, is directed against the judgment
and order dated 15.07.2008, passed by Additional
Sessions Judge/Ist Fast Track Court, Rudrapur,
Udham Singh Nagar, in Sessions Trial No. 208 of

2
2006, whereby said court has convicted the
accused/appellant Ravidas under section 376 of
I.P.C., and sentenced him to rigorous
imprisonment for a period of seven years and
directed to pay fine of ` 5,000/-. In default of
payment of fine the convict has been directed to
undergo further imprisonment for a period of six
months by the trial court.
(2) Heard learned Amicus Curiae for the
appellant, and learned counsel for the State, and
also perused the lower court record.
(3) Prosecution story, in brief, is that PW4 Ms.
Nikita was aged about four years, and accused
Ravidas (appellant) was aged about sixty years
who used to live in her neighbourhood in the
village Tagore Nagar, within the limits of Police
Station Sitarganj in District Udham Singh Nagar.
On 18.06.2006, at about 11.00 am, he took Ms.
Nikita, with him by giving her allurement that he
would give her EGG and SAMOSA. PW1 Parwati,
mother of PW2 Ms. Nikita heard shrieks on her
daughter and went to the house of accused
Ravidas, who was committing rape on her. The
accused Ravidas on seing PW1 Parwati got up and

3
threw the girl on the ground from the cot. Since
PW1 Parwati was all alone in her house she
waited till her father in law, who was a carpenter
came back in the house in the evening. Thereafter
she got dictated First Information Report (Ex-A1)
and gave it at Police Outpost Shakti Farm of
Police Station Sitarganj, on the very day. On the
basis of said report Crime No. 970 of 2006 was
registered at Police Station Sitarganj, against the
accused Ravidas in respect of offence punishable
under section 376 of I.P.C. PW5 Sub Inspector
K.R.Pandey took up the investigation. The little
girl was medically examined by PW2 Dr. Titiksha
of female hospital Sitarganj. She observed in her
report (Ex-A3) that Ms. Nikita might be victim of
attempted rape as the tenderness was found in
vulval region and out side the hymen area. As to
the age of the girl she advised X-ray of elbow and
wrist of the girl. No sign of violence in the form of
bruises or laceration was found on the person of
the girl. Only on the local area oedema of
tenderness was found present. Supplementary
reports (Ex-A4 and Ex-A5) prepared by PW2 Dr.
Titiksha, after receiving the X-ray report and
pathological report show that the age of the girl
(Nikita) was between 3 to 5 years, and no dead

4
and alive spermatozoa seen. After interrogating the
witness and inspecting the spot, the Investigating
Officer submitted charge sheet (Ex-A7) against
accused Ravidas for his trial in respect of offence
punishable under section 376 of I.P.C.
(4) The Judicial Magistrate, Khatima, on receipt
of the charge sheet after giving necessary copies to
the accused as required under section 207 of
Cr.P.C, appears to have committed the case to the
court of Sessions for trial. On 22.03.2007, the trial
court after hearing the parties framed charge of
offence punishable under section 376 of I.P.C.,
against accused Ravidas, who pleaded not guilty
and claimed to be tried. On this, prosecution got
examined PW1 Parwati (informant and mother of
the victim), PW2 Dr. Titiksha (who medically
examined the girl), PW3 Ajay Jaiswal (who
scribed the report), PW4 Ms. Nikita (victim) and
PW5 Sub Inspector K.R.Pandey (Investigating
Officer). The oral and documentary evidence was
put to the accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C, in
reply to which he pleaded that the evidence
adduced against him was false. He further pleaded
that mother of the girl and grand father of the girl
wanted to occupy temple land and the

5
accused/appellant Ravidas opposed the same due
to which he has been falsely implicated. However,
no evidence in defence was adduced. The trial
court after hearing the parties, found that
prosecution has successfully proved charge of
offence punishable under section 376 of I.P.C.
After hearing on sentence, the convict was
sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for a period
of seven years and directed to pay fine of `
5,000/- by the trial court. In default of payment of
fine the convict was directed to undergo further
imprisonment for a period of six months.
Aggrieved by said judgment and order dated
15.07.2008, passed by Additional Sessions
Judge/Ist Fast Track Court, Rudrapur, Udham
Singh Nagar, in Sessions Trial No. 208 of 2006, ,
this appeal was got sent by the convict from jail.
(5) Before further discussion this Court thinks
it just and proper to mention the observations made
by PW2 Dr. Titiksha, who prepared medical report
(Ex-A3) after examining the little girl Nikita on
19.06.2006. Her observations are being reproduced
below :-
" Examination (External):- No sign of
violence in the form of bruises or laceration

6
present on the body. On local area oedema
of tenderness is present.
Axillary hair not present. Genital hair not
present.
Breast are not developed as puberty is not
reached.
Internal Examination :- Labia minora not
developed.
Secretions are not seen on surface.
 On little finger per vaginal examination.
Little finger cannot be admitted and no sign
of hymen tear are present. Although
tenderness is present.
Slide is made from the secretions
obtained round the
area...............................................................
Opinion :- (i) Patient may be a victim of
attempt to rape as tenderness is present in
vulval region and outside the hymen area. But
it could be certainly said only after the smear
examination.
(ii) As far as age is concerned X ray of
elbow and wrist are mandatory."
Supplementary report prepared by PW2 Dr.
Titiksha (Ex-A4) shows that no dead or alive

7
spermatozoa were seen. Ex-A5 shows that in view
of radiological examination the age of the girl
could be between 3 to 5 years.
(6) Now, this Court has to examine the ocular
testimony of the victim (PW4). PW4 Ms. Nikita
was examined by the trial court and when the
court came to the conclusion that she is able to
understand the question and to answer, her
statement was recorded. PW4 Ms. Nikita has
stated that accused Ravidas lives in the neighbour
behind her house. She further told that accused
Ravidas undressed her. She further told that after
making her lay down on a cot accused kept on
drawing her again and again (to his body). She
further told that accused inserted his genital into
her genital. In the cross examination the witness
has stated the she felt pain below her belly due to
the act on the part of accused. She further stated
that the accused gave her SAMOSA . She also told
that accused Ravidas took her from her house
promising her that he would give her EGG. She
also told in the cross examination that at the time
she was taken by the accused, her mother was
stitching a quilt. She admitted no MARPEET was
done by the accused. PW4 Ms. Nikita further told

8
that after she shouted, her mother and other
neighbours came there. The above statement of the
girl is natural and trustworthy and supported by the
medical evidence discussed above.
(7) PW1 Parwati, mother of the victim has
further corroborated the prosecution story. She has
further proved the First Information Report (Ex-A1) got lodged by her. PW3 Ajay Jaiswal, has
proved the fact that on dictation of PW1 Parwati
he scribed the report.
(8) Having re-appreciated the entire evidence on
record, this court finds that trial court has rightly
found that the prosecution has successfully proved
charge of offence punishable under section 376 of
I.P.C., against accused Ravidas.
(9) Learned Amicus Curiae on behalf of the
appellant argued that it is a case of attempt to
commit rape, and not that of commission of rape.
However, on going through the definition of rape
this Court found that partial penetration also
constitutes rape. The injury suffered on the private
part by the little child sufficiently established that
the rape was committed on her. As far as, the

9
sentence awarded by the trial court is concerned,
the same is appears to be lenient in the facts and
circumstances of the case, as such, no interference
is required with the impugned judgment and
order passed by the trial court.
(10) Therefore, the appeal is dismissed.
Conviction and sentence recorded by the trial court
(Additional Sessions Judge/Ist Fast Track Court,
Udham Singh Nagar) in Sessions Trial No. 208 of
2006, under section 376 of I.P.C, against the
accused/appellant Ravidas is hereby affirmed.
Lower court record be sent back. Let a copy of
this judgment be sent to the Superintendent of the
jail concerned.
(Prafulla C. Pant, J.)
21.03.2013
N.P
